stem: Two lines intersect. One of the four angles formed measures $38^\circ$. What is the measure, in degrees, of an angle adjacent to it?
explanation: Neighbouring angles at an intersection add to $180^\circ$, so the adjacent angle is $180-38=142$.

stem: In the figure, $A$, $P$ and $B$ lie on a line. What is the value of $x$?
explanation: $A$, $P$, $B$ lie on a straight line, so the two angles add to $180^\circ$: $2x+3x=180$, $5x=180$, $x=36$.

stem: In the figure, lines $k$ and $m$ are parallel. What is the value of $x$?
explanation: Because $k\parallel m$, every angle is either $65^\circ$ or $y^\circ$ with $65+y=180$. The angle marked $x$ lies on the opposite side of the transversal from the neighbouring $65^\circ$ angle, so $x=180-65=115$.

choiceExplanations.A: That is $90-65$; nothing in the figure makes a right angle.
choiceExplanations.B: The angle marked $x^\circ$ is not equal to the $65^\circ$ angle; it is its supplement.
choiceExplanations.D: That is $180+65$; an angle at a line crossing is less than $180^\circ$.
choiceExplanations.E: That is $360-65$, the reflex angle, not the angle marked.

stem: Lines $k$ and $m$ are parallel and are crossed by a third line. One of the eight angles formed measures $50^\circ$. Which of the following could be the measure of another of the eight angles? Indicate all such measures.
explanation: Four angles equal $50^\circ$ and the other four equal $180-50=130$. So $50^\circ$ and $130^\circ$ occur.

choiceExplanations.C: A right angle would make all eight angles $90^\circ$, not $50^\circ$.
choiceExplanations.E: Each of the eight angles is less than $180^\circ$.

stem: Points $P$, $Q$, $R$ and $S$ lie in that order on a line. $PR=18$, $QS=22$, and $Q$ is the midpoint of $PR$. What is the length of $RS$?
explanation: $Q$ is the midpoint of $PR$, so $QR=9$. Since $Q,R,S$ are in order, $QS=QR+RS$, giving $RS=22-9=13$.

stem: Two lines intersect. Two opposite angles measure $(4a+6)^\circ$ and $(7a-39)^\circ$. What is the measure of an angle adjacent to the $(4a+6)^\circ$ angle?
explanation: Opposite angles are equal: $4a+6=7a-39$, so $3a=45$ and $a=15$. Each of those angles is $4(15)+6=66^\circ$. An adjacent angle is $180-66=114^\circ$.

choiceExplanations.A: That is the value of $a$, not an angle.
choiceExplanations.B: That is the opposite angle itself; an adjacent angle is its supplement.

stem: In the figure, lines $k$ and $m$ are parallel. What is the value of $x$?
explanation: The two marked angles are not equal: they are a $110^\circ$-type and a $70^\circ$-type angle, so they add to $180$. $(3x+5)+(x+35)=180$ gives $4x=140$, $x=35$. Check: $110^\circ$ and $70^\circ$.

stem: Three lines intersect at a single point, forming six angles. Three angles that are consecutive around the point measure $x^\circ$, $2x^\circ$ and $3x^\circ$. What is the measure of the largest of the six angles?
explanation: Opposite angles are equal, so the six angles are $x,2x,3x,x,2x,3x$ and add to $360^\circ$: $12x=360$, $x=30$. The largest is $3x=90^\circ$.

choiceExplanations.D: No angle of $120^\circ$ occurs: the six angles are 30, 60, 90, 30, 60, 90.
choiceExplanations.E: That comes from using $x+2x+3x=360$; but those three angles span only a straight line, so they add to $180$.

stem: Points $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ lie in that order on a line. $M$ is the midpoint of $AB$, $N$ is the midpoint of $CD$, $BC=12$ and $MN=30$. What is the value of $AB+CD$?
explanation: $MN=MB+BC+CN=\tfrac12AB+12+\tfrac12CD=30$. So $\tfrac12(AB+CD)=18$ and $AB+CD=36$.

stem: Four angles are arranged around a single point so that together they fill the whole turn. Three of them measure $70^\circ$, $85^\circ$ and $110^\circ$. What is the measure, in degrees, of the fourth angle?
explanation: Angles around a point add up to $360^\circ$, so the fourth angle is $360-(70+85+110)=360-265=95$.

stem: Two lines intersect, and two adjacent angles formed by them are in the ratio $2:7$. What is the measure of the smaller of these two angles?
explanation: Adjacent angles at an intersection form a straight line, so they add to $180^\circ$. The ratio $2:7$ makes $2+7=9$ equal parts, each $180\div9=20^\circ$. The smaller angle has 2 parts: $40^\circ$.

choiceExplanations.A: $20^\circ$ is a single part; the smaller angle is made of 2 parts.
choiceExplanations.C: This divides $360^\circ$, not $180^\circ$, into nine parts; adjacent angles add to $180^\circ$.
choiceExplanations.D: $140^\circ$ is the larger of the two angles, not the smaller.
choiceExplanations.E: This is $7$ parts of $360\div9$; it uses $360^\circ$ and picks the larger angle.

stem: Compare Quantity A and Quantity B, using additional information centered above the two quantities if such information is given.
explanation: Adjacent angles lie on a straight line, so Quantity A is always $180^\circ$. Opposite angles are equal, so Quantity B is twice the measure $x$ of one angle, which equals $180$ only when $x=90$ (perpendicular lines). For other crossings $2x$ is below or above 180, so the relationship cannot be determined.

content.quantityB: The sum of the measures of two opposite angles

stem: In the figure, lines $k$ and $m$ are parallel and are crossed by line $p$. Angle 1 measures $110^\circ$. Which of the numbered angles measure $70^\circ$? Indicate all such angles.
explanation: Angle 1 is obtuse, so with parallel lines every obtuse angle (1, 3, 5 and 7) measures $110^\circ$ and every acute angle (2, 4, 6 and 8) measures $180-110=70^\circ$. Of the listed angles, 2, 6 and 8 are acute.

choiceExplanations.B: Angle 3 is vertical to angle 1 (opposite it), so it also measures $110^\circ$.
choiceExplanations.C: Angle 5 sits in the same position at the lower crossing as angle 1 at the upper one, so it also measures $110^\circ$.

stem: Points $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ lie in that order on a line. $B$ is the midpoint of $AC$, and $C$ is the midpoint of $BD$. If $AD=45$, what is the length of $BC$?
explanation: Since $B$ is the midpoint of $AC$, $AB=BC$. Since $C$ is the midpoint of $BD$, $BC=CD$. So $AD=AB+BC+CD=3\cdot BC=45$ and $BC=15$.

stem: In the figure, lines $k$ and $m$ are parallel. The marked angles measure $(3x-10)^\circ$ and $(2x+50)^\circ$. What is the measure of the angle marked $(2x+50)^\circ$?
explanation: The angle marked $(3x-10)^\circ$ equals the angle in the same position at the lower crossing, and that angle and the one marked $(2x+50)^\circ$ lie on a straight line. So $(3x-10)+(2x+50)=180$, $5x=140$, $x=28$. The marked angle measures $2(28)+50=106^\circ$.

choiceExplanations.A: $28$ is the value of $x$, not the measure of the marked angle.
choiceExplanations.E: This comes from setting the two expressions equal ($x=60$); the angles are supplementary, not equal.

stem: In the figure, $F$ is the point of line $\ell$ nearest to $P$, so $PF$ is perpendicular to $\ell$. $Q$ and $R$ are points of $\ell$ on opposite sides of $F$. If $PF=8$, $PQ=10$ and $PR=17$, what is the length of $QR$?
explanation: Triangles $PFQ$ and $PFR$ are right triangles with the right angle at $F$. $FQ=\sqrt{10^2-8^2}=6$ and $FR=\sqrt{17^2-8^2}=\sqrt{225}=15$. As $Q$ and $R$ are on opposite sides of $F$, $QR=6+15=21$.

stem: Lines $k$ and $m$ are parallel and are crossed by a third line. Two of the eight angles formed measure $(7x-4)^\circ$ and $(2x+31)^\circ$. What is the sum of all possible values of $x$?
explanation: Any two of the eight angles are either equal or add up to $180^\circ$. Equal: $7x-4=2x+31$ gives $x=7$ (both angles $45^\circ$). Supplementary: $(7x-4)+(2x+31)=180$ gives $9x=153$, $x=17$ (angles $115^\circ$ and $65^\circ$). Both values are valid, so the sum is $7+17=24$.
